To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spaceflight impairs the ability of skeletal muscle resistance arterioles to contract in response to vasoconstrictors and stretch-activated mechanisms.
the reduced vasoconstriction to vasoactive stimuli and the reduced contractility in skeletal muscle resistance arteries after spaceflight may be due to reduced expression of ryanodine receptors.
the reduced vasoconstriction in mouse skeletal muscle arteries following spaceflight is due to a deficit in calcium release via ryanodine receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of spaceflight on the contractile properties of the microcirculation.
understanding the mechanisms of cardiovascular deconditioning in humans after space travel and how these changes may contribute to cardiovascular risk in astronauts and cosmonauts.
the mechanisms of cardiovascular adaptation to microgravity and how the body adapts to return to Earth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spaceflight-induced reduction in vascular reactivity of the skeletal muscle microcirculation is associated with a decrease in the contractile response of the smooth muscle cells, which is likely due to a reduction in the expression of the ryanodine receptors RyR-2, RyR-3.
the spaceflight-associated changes in vascular reactivity are likely due to a decrease in the sensitivity of the vascular smooth muscle to vasoconstriction.
spaceflight reduced the contractility of the resistance arteries in the skeletal muscles of mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spaceflight environment reduces vasoconstriction in skeletal muscle resistance vessels by reducing calcium signaling through RyR-2, RyR-3, and SERCA-2.

spaceflight-induced changes in the contractile properties of skeletal muscle resistance vessels may contribute to the orthostatic intolerance observed in spaceflight subjects upon return to terrestrial conditions.
spaceflight impairs the contractile capacity of skeletal muscle arteries, thereby reducing the capacity to respond to vasoconstrictive challenges upon return to 1G.
The main takeaway from our work is that
skeletal muscle resistance arteries from mice flown in space have reduced vasoconstriction responses to adrenergic and stretch-activated stimuli compared to those of ground controls.
spaceflight reduces vasocontractile responses of skeletal muscle resistance vessels, which may be due to impaired intracellular Ca(2+) handling.
spaceflight impairs the ability to constrict resistance arteries, and the mechanism is a reduction in the sensitivity of the sarcoplasmic reticulum to release Ca(2+).
